definitions.explanation: The most severe legal punishment, in which the convicted person is sentenced to death. Japan retains the death penalty, carried out by hanging.

examples.japanese: {被告|ひこく}に{死刑|しけい}が{言|い}い{渡|わた}された。
examples.english: The defendant was sentenced to death.

examples.japanese: {死刑|しけい}{制度|せいど}の{廃止|はいし}を{求|もと}める{声|こえ}が{高|たか}まっている。
examples.english: There is growing demand for the abolition of the death penalty.

examples.japanese: {死刑|しけい}に{賛成|さんせい}か{反対|はんたい}かは{国|くに}によって{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれる{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.english: Whether one supports or opposes the death penalty is an issue on which opinions differ by country.

notes:
USAGE:
Japan is one of the few developed countries that retains the death penalty. The topic frequently appears in news and social studies materials. {死刑|しけい}{執行|しっこう} (execution of the death penalty) is carried out by the Minister of Justice's order.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {死刑|しけい}{判決|はんけつ}: death sentence
- {死刑|しけい}{制度|せいど}: death penalty system
- {死刑|しけい}{執行|しっこう}: execution
- {死刑|しけい}{廃止|はいし}: abolition of the death penalty
- {死刑|しけい}{囚|しゅう}: death row inmate
- {死刑|しけい}を{求刑|きゅうけい}する: to demand the death penalty (prosecution)
